Package neqsim.thermo.util.mercury

Class MercuryPhaseEquilibrium

java.lang.Object
neqsim.thermo.util.mercury.MercuryPhaseEquilibrium
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable
public final class MercuryPhaseEquilibrium extends Object implements Serializable
Phase equilibrium of a fluid with a separate elemental mercury phase.

The fluid phases (gas, oil, aqueous) are in equilibrium with pure condensed mercury when the fluid holds more mercury than it can dissolve. The mercury phase is treated as pure: liquid above the melting point and solid below it. Its fugacity is the pure liquid fugacity from the equation of state of the fluid, corrected below the melting point with the enthalpy of fusion and the pressure effect on the solid.

Mercury is treated as a dilute solute. The split of the other components comes from a flash at trace mercury content, and the mercury content of each phase is then solved so that mercury has the same fugacity in all fluid phases, limited by the pure mercury fugacity. The error from this is of the order of the dissolved mercury mole fraction, which is normally below 1e-5.

The calculation works on a copy of the fluid taken when the object is created; the fluid given to the constructor is not changed, and later changes to it are not seen by this object.

1.0

Even Solbraa
